title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
Stanford published banners carrying an AI-altered photograph of a real, named student, Billy Ramirez, whose likeness was replaced with an image of a Black woman, while two other students in the same photograph were made to look thinner. The edit was applied to an existing photo of identifiable people and then used in university materials, so the failure sits at the point where a synthetic image entered public-facing output. This is an undisclosed substitution of a person's identity, not a model asserting a false fact in text.

Catching it required two things the process did not have: a check of the final image against the original photograph before publication, and disclosure that AI had been used. Stanford's own policy bans using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements, and the university has said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. The student learned about the change from a friend, and Stanford has said it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and to make sure all materials are properly reviewed.

What is not established is who performed the edit, whether the alteration was intended, or whether anyone faced consequences, since a confirmed policy violation is not by itself a finding of deliberate deception.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford photographer took a photo of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The dining service posted it online. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to alter the original image. The university said its policy bans using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and make sure all materials are properly reviewed.
